articles.title: Important Indian Space Missions and Collaborations with Foreign Agencies - GKToday
articles.content: Home Important Indian Space Missions and Collaborations with Foreign Agencies Important Indian Space Missions and Collaborations with Foreign Agencies The Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) conducts space exploration, satellite launches, and scientific research. India operates lunar, interplanetary, solar, and earth observation missions independently as well as in partnership with international space agencies. These international collaborations involve payload sharing, joint satellite development, deep space tracking, and astronaut training programs. Lunar and Planetary Exploration Missions India’s planetary program includes missions to the Moon and Mars to study surface composition, atmospheric dynamics, and mineralogy. Chandrayaan Series Chandrayaan-1 (2008): Launched aboard PSLV-C11, it was India’s first lunar probe. It carried eleven scientific instruments, including five from India, two from NASA, three from the European Space Agency (ESA), and one from Bulgaria. The Moon Mineralogy Mapper (M3) from NASA confirmed the presence of water molecules on the lunar surface. Chandrayaan-2 (2019): Launched using GSLV Mk III-M1, consisting of an orbiter, the Vikram lander, and the Pragyan rover. While the lander crashed during soft landing attempts, the orbiter remains operational in lunar orbit. Chandrayaan-3 (2023): Successfully executed a soft landing near the lunar south polar region on August 23, 2023. It deployed the Vikram lander and Pragyan rover to analyze lunar soil composition and seismic activity. The landing site was named Shiv Shakti Point. Mars Orbiter Mission (Mangalyaan) Launched in November 2013 on PSLV-C25, the Mars Orbiter Mission entered Martian orbit in September 2014. It made ISRO the fourth space agency to reach Mars orbit. The spacecraft carried five indigenous instruments, including the Mars Colour Camera and the Thermal Infrared Imaging Spectrometer. Solar and Space Astronomy Observatories India operates space observatories to study cosmic radiation, stellar dynamics, and solar processes. AstroSat (2015) AstroSat is India’s first dedicated multi-wavelength space observatory. Launched aboard PSLV-C30, it monitors the universe simultaneously in ultraviolet, optical, low-energy X-ray, and high-energy X-ray wavebands. The mission involved collaborations with the Canadian Space Agency and the University of Leicester. Aditya-L1 (2023) Aditya-L1 is India’s first space-based observatory placed in a halo orbit around the Sun-Earth Lagrange Point 1 (L1), located approximately 1.5 million kilometers from Earth. It carries seven payloads to study the solar corona, chromosphere, photosphere, and solar wind particles. Mission Launch Year Target Body / Orbit Key Objective Chandrayaan-1 2008 Lunar Polar Orbit High-resolution mineralogical and chemical mapping Mars Orbiter Mission 2013 Martian Orbit Surface features and atmospheric morphology AstroSat 2015 Low Earth Orbit Multi-wavelength observation of celestial sources Chandrayaan-3 2023 Lunar South Pole In-situ thermal and seismic surface analysis Aditya-L1 2023 Sun-Earth L1 Halo Orbit Solar coronal heating and coronal mass ejections XPoSat 2024 Low Earth Orbit Polarimetry of cosmic X-ray sources Human Spaceflight: Gaganyaan The Gaganyaan program aims to demonstrate Indian human spaceflight capability to Low Earth Orbit. Mission Profile: Designed to carry a crew of three astronauts to a 400-kilometer orbit for a three-day mission and bring them safely back to Earth with a splashdown in Indian sea waters. articles.title: EY India and Shri Ram College of Commerce (SRCC) launch AI VIBE to prepare students ...
articles.content: Technology For SMEs IoT & AI EY India and Shri Ram College of Commerce (SRCC) launch AI VIBE to prepare students for AI-enabled careers The EY-sponsored programme will be open to students from SRCC (Semester 3 onwards) and will follow a selective admissions process comprising assessments, interviews and submission of a Statement of Purpose (SOP). SMEStreet Edit Desk 18 Aug 2026 15:12 IST Follow Us New Update Listen to this article 0.75x 1x 1.5x 00:00 / 00:00 EY India and Shri Ram College of Commerce (SRCC) announced the launch of AI VIBE (Varsity for Innovation, Business and Economics), a first-of-its-kind immersive industry-academia initiative aimed at preparing students for careers in an AI-enabled economy. Jointly developed by SRCC and EY India, the 12-month programme combines academic excellence with industry immersion to help bridge the growing gap between classroom learning and the AI skills increasingly required in today's workplace. The EY-sponsored programme will be open to students from SRCC (Semester 3 onwards) and will follow a selective admissions process comprising assessments, interviews and submission of a Statement of Purpose (SOP). During the duration of the course, participants will be evaluated through continuous project-based assessments and a final evaluation. As organizations increasingly integrate AI into core business processes, reskilling and AI literacy are becoming essential for success in entry-level roles. AI VIBE participants will receive immersive training in machine learning, Generative AI, AI agents, decision intelligence, data analytics, financial technologies, blockchain, responsible AI and AI governance, equipping them with the skills needed to thrive in a rapidly evolving business environment. Rajiv Memani, Chairman and CEO, EY India, said “At a time when AI is transforming businesses and the workplace, while creating demand for the skills of the future, students must view AI literacy as a foundational capability and cultivate it through continuous learning and curiosity. Through AI VIBE, we are helping shape the next generation of talent and leaders in India, beginning with SRCC, one of the country's premier undergraduate institutions. By combining academic excellence in AI with practical business experience, we aim to help students build the capabilities they need to thrive in the age of AI.” The curriculum will be enriched through hackathons, mentoring, industry engagement and applied learning experiences designed to strengthen both technical expertise and business problem-solving capabilities. Students will learn from leading AI specialists from EY India and industry professionals. Prof. Simrit Kaur, Principal, Shri Ram College of Commerce, University of Delhi, said, "Higher education is entering a period of profound change, by connecting education with industry, we are bridging the skills gap and enabling students to enter the workforce with greater confidence and readiness. Through AI VIBE, SRCC and EY India are collaborating to create a new learning model that goes beyond traditional classroom instruction and enables students to engage with real-world business challenges, industry practitioners and emerging technologies in a structured and meaningful way. This will further elevate the learning and experience for the students. Indeed, a progressive initiative by SRCC in its Centenary!" With an...

articles.title: iQOO Hackathon 2026 launched as India's first hybrid mobile development challenge
articles.content: iQOO has launched the iQOO Hackathon 2026, billed as India’s first hybrid mobile hackathon. Targeted at software engineers, student developers, AI enthusiasts, and early-career IT professionals, the competition tasks participants with developing technology solutions for real-world problems using a mobile-first workflow. Format and Development Model The hackathon introduces a hybrid structure requiring participants to integrate smartphones directly into traditional development environments. “Red Light, Green Light” Workflow: During designated “Red Light” phases, teams must develop and code primarily on an iQOO 15 smartphone. During “Green Light” phases, participants may blend mobile tasks with conventional laptop development. Hardware Utilization: The challenge leverages the iQOO 15’s hardware profile—including its Snapdragon processor, OriginOS optimizations, integrated vapor cooling system, and extended battery capacity—to test mobile feasibility for sustained programming workloads. Evaluation Criteria: Projects will be evaluated by an industry panel of AI specialists and technology executives on phone-first execution, AI integration, Office Kit utilization, real-world utility, and pitch quality. Participants will receive dedicated AI credits and guidance from over a dozen industry mentors. Schedule and Regional Battles The competition follows a 30-hour regional format across four major technology hubs before concluding with a national finale in Bengaluru. Stage / Location Dates Scope Bengaluru City Battle August 29–30, 2026 Regional qualifier Pune City Battle September 5–6, 2026 Regional qualifier Chennai City Battle September 12–13, 2026 Regional qualifier Hyderabad City Battle September 26–27, 2026 Regional qualifier Grand Finale (Bengaluru) October 9–11, 2026 National championship Prize Pool and Registration Each regional City Battle carries a prize pool of ₹6 lakh , distributed among the Winner, First Runner-up, Second Runner-up, Special Honour recipients, and standout projects. Winners from each regional round and select shortlisted candidates from online submissions will advance to the Grand Finale in Bengaluru to compete for a separate ₹25 lakh national prize pool. Registrations are currently open to eligible developers and students through the official portal at iqoo.reskilll.com . articles.title: Agent B Studio Launches India's First Agentic AI Platform for the Interior Design industry
articles.content: Technology For SMEs IoT & AI Agent B Studio Launches India's First Agentic AI Platform for the Interior Design industry Agent B Studio today announced its Visual AI platform, designed to bring the entire design workflow into one connected system. Powered by a multimodal AI orchestration engine, the platform enables architects, SMEStreet Edit Desk 18 Aug 2026 14:34 IST Follow Us New Update Listen to this article 0.75x 1x 1.5x 00:00 / 00:00 While generative AI has transformed content creation, the $800 billion+ interiors and furnishings industry still relies on fragmented software, manual documentation and disconnected workflows. Designers continue to manage separate tools for planning, rendering, sourcing and client delivery, while brands struggle to participate earlier in the purchase journey. Agent B Studio today announced its Visual AI platform, designed to bring the entire design workflow into one connected system. Powered by a multimodal AI orchestration engine, the platform enables architects, interior designers, furniture brands and real estate developers to design, visualize, specify and deliver projects through a single workflow. Unlike conventional AI image generators, Agent B Studio generates spatially accurate photorealistic renders from real floor plans and dimensions. Its AI-powered tools, including Layout to Render, Quick Generate, Smart Project, Photo Edit, and Bella, its AI assistant help users create layouts, customize spaces, integrate real products, and generate documentation, quotations and presentations. Beyond visualization, Agent B Studio connects design with commerce by enabling brands to bring their product catalogs directly into the design process, helping influence purchasing decisions at the point where they are made. The platform has crossed 5,000+ designer signups within ten weeks of launch, with professionals adopting Agent B Studio as an end-to-end workflow solution. Founded by Natasha Jain, Agent B Studio is built from more than a decade of firsthand experience in the interiors industry. Before launching the platform, Natasha founded Bent Chair, one of India’s leading premium furniture brands, and Natelier, its luxury design house. Her experience revealed a fundamental gap: while design creativity evolved, the technology powering workflows remained fragmented. Before entering the design industry, Natasha founded fintech startup Ruplee, which was later acquired by Paylo. A Georgia Tech-trained Industrial Engineer with a Master's in Management Science & Engineering from Stanford University, she brings together experience across engineering, entrepreneurship and design. "For years, the industry has had to choose between speed and accuracy, relying on disconnected tools and manual workflows. Agent B Studio brings design, visualization and delivery together through an AI-powered platform, making professional workflows faster and more accessible," said Natasha Jain, Founder & CEO, Agent B Studio. Agent B Studio aims to become the operating system for the global interiors economy, connecting design, visualization, products, sourcing and commerce through one intelligent platform. articles.title: Police personnel of all ranks should get Rajahamsa bus travel facility urges ... - Country and Politics
articles.content: Pramesh S Jain Karnataka State Police Complaints Authority member Mohan Kumar Danappa has urged the Director General and Inspector General of Police (DG&IGP) to extend the existing KSRTC Rajahamsa bus travel facility,available to police inspectors and senior officers,to police personnel of all ranks travelling on official duty. In a representation submitted to the DGP on Monday, Danappa said police personnel from districts such as Bidar,Belagavi,Vijayapura,Kalaburagi,Yadgir,Karwar, Udupi,Mangaluru,Koppal,Ballari,Vijayanagara and Raichur frequently travel 400–500 km to Bengaluru and back for official assignments. He said personnel are often required to report for duty immediately after completing long-distance journeys, resulting in considerable physical and mental fatigue. Police personnel deployed for law-and-order duties, bandobast,investigations and emergency assignments are already working under considerable pressure,he noted. According to Danappa,the Rajahamsa travel facility is presently available to police inspectors and officers above that rank on a warrant basis. However,he pointed out that around 80% of inspectors travelling on outside-duty assignments are provided departmental vehicles such as Boleros,reducing their dependence on the warrant facility. “Lower-ranking personnel, including those who have served for 20–25 years as well as younger personnel, often have to undertake long journeys in ordinary buses,” he said,highlighting the physical strain caused by prolonged travel. The representation also cited health concerns among police personnel,including back pain,physical and mental stress caused by prolonged sitting and the impact of irregular working hours and inadequate leave. Danappa said police personnel are increasingly facing lifestyle and stress-related health problems and that instances of premature deaths before retirement were a matter of concern for the department. He urged the police department to consider the request from the perspective of personnel welfare and extend warrant-based travel on KSRTC Rajahamsa buses to police personnel of all ranks travelling on official duty. Danappa said the measure would improve the health, safety,physical fitness and overall efficiency of police personnel,besides improving the quality of their work.

articles.content: home Spotlight News wire Story tv launches india s first hybrid ai drama the bose network bringing netaji s1940 s story to life Story TV Launches India’s First Hybrid AI Drama ‘The Bose Network’, Bringing Netaji’s 1940’s Story To Life Four countries, multiple identities, secret radio broadcasts, wartime missions, and a submarine crossing, recreated for a new generation of vertical storytelling. PNN Updated on: 17 August 2026 7:50 pm Published At: 17 August 2026 7:49 pm Updated on: 17 August 2026 7:50 pm Published At: 17 August 2026 7:49 pm SUBSCRIBE Story TV Launches India’s First Hybrid AI Drama ‘The Bose Network’, Bringing Netaji’s 1940’s Story To Life Mumbai (Maharashtra) [India], August 17: Story TV, India’s leading microdrama platform from the Eloelo Group, premiered its latest series, The Bose Network, at midnight on August 15. The historical thriller is India’s first title built on an AI-integrated production pipeline, marking a significant step in Story TV’s ambition to build a premium slate for vertical storytelling. The Bose Network expands the creative possibilities of the vertical format, bringing a richly detailed period world to the screen at an unprecedented scale. Set across the 1940s, the series recreates Calcutta, the Frontier Kabul, wartime Berlin and the interiors of two submarines, taking audiences across four countries and four years of wartime history. Eloelo Group’s AI expertise was used extensively in post-production to build these environments, enabling the storytelling to move seamlessly across geographies, eras and settings. The approach also opens up a new production model for premium vertical storytelling. By building period environments in post-production, greater creative focus can be placed on writing, casting, performances and sound. More importantly, the AI-integrated pipeline becomes a reusable platform capability, creating a foundation for Story TV to develop a wider range of ambitious, premium stories across genres and settings. 1 August 2026 Get the latest issue of Outlook Business AI is now central to Story TV’s production strategy, contributing to 50% of its production workflow, with the platform targeting 1,000+ AI-powered shows by the end of this fiscal. The focus is on using AI not just to scale production, but to expand the ambition, visual quality and diversity of premium vertical storytelling. articles.title: Light To Moderate Rain With Thunder Likely In 10 Odisha Dists In Next 3 Hrs
articles.content: Bhubaneswar : The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a nowcast warning to 10 Odisha districts, cautioning residents of light to moderate rain accompanied by thunder and lightning. According to the alert released at 10:10 on Tuesday, rain with thunderstorm activity is very likely at a few places over the districts of Kendujhar, Sundaragada, Nuapada, Anugola, Debagada, Sambalpur, Bargada, Balangir, Jharsuguda and Mayurbhanj during the next three hours. The IMD has advised people in the affected areas to remain alert, monitor weather updates closely, and take necessary precautions for their safety. Tags: IMD Nowcast Warning

articles.title: India, League of Arab States reaffirm commitment to strengthen partnership - IANS LIVE
articles.content: India, League of Arab States reaffirm commitment to strengthen partnership IANS August 17, 2026 10:39 PM Share on | Cairo, Aug 17 (IANS) Sripriya Ranganathan, Secretary (Consular, Passport and Visa and Overseas Indian Affairs) at the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA), met Amb Khalid Manzalawi, Assistant Secretary-General of the League of Arab States, on Monday and reaffirmed the commitment to strengthen the partnership. “Secretary (CPV and OIA) Ms Sripriya Ranganathan met H.E. Amb Khalid Manzalawi, Assistant Secretary-General of the League of Arab States. Discussions focused on advancing the Executive Programme 2026-28, adopted at the 2nd India-Arab Foreign Ministers’ Meeting, including through concrete initiatives in new and emerging areas of cooperation. Both sides reaffirmed their commitment to further strengthening the India-Arab partnership,” the Indian Embassy in Egypt stated on X. On Sunday, the Secretary highlighted the priorities of India's BRICS 2026 Chairship at the India-Egypt BRICS Partnership Conference. "Sripriya Ranganathan addressed the Inaugural Session of the India-Egypt BRICS Partnership Conference, organised by the Indian Embassy in Egypt in collaboration with the Indian Council of World Affairs, at the Diplomatic Club in Cairo," the Indian Embassy in Egypt said on social media platform X on Sunday. "Secretary Ranganathan highlighted the priorities of India's BRICS 2026 Chairship and underscored how the India-Egypt Strategic Partnership provides a strong foundation for closer cooperation within BRICS and for advancing the priorities of the Global South," it added. Secretary Ranganathan is on an official visit to Egypt, Palestine and Lebanon from August 16-21. According to the MEA, during her visit, Secretary Ranganathan will meet her counterparts and various stakeholders. "The visit will focus on reinforcing India's friendly ties with these countries and also offer an opportunity for discussions on regional developments and other issues of mutual interest," the Ministry said. The MEA also said this is the Secretary's maiden visit to these countries in her current capacity and is expected to strengthen India's ties with the region further. --IANS ksk/dan

articles.title: Centre clears 31 more ECMS projects; approved investment crosses Rs 69,500 crore
articles.content: NEW DELHI: The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) on Monday approved 31 new projects under the Electronics Component Manufacturing Scheme (ECMS), taking the total number of cleared proposals to 106 and pushing the cumulative approved investment beyond Rs 69,500 crore. The latest approvals mark India's first domestic manufacturing of several critical electronic components, including filters, coils and speakers, besides key raw materials such as acetylene black and electrolyte additives. Minister for Electronics and Information Technology Ashwini Vaishnaw said 38 plants approved under the scheme have already started manufacturing, while another 16 are in advanced stages of construction or machinery installation. The approved projects are expected to generate around 75,000 direct jobs and strengthen India's electronics supply chain by reducing import dependence across multiple component categories. Vaishnaw said India's manufacturing capacity for electronic enclosures now meets nearly 100% of domestic demand, making the country "fully Aatmanirbhar" in the segment. He added that production capacities have already surpassed domestic demand in several component categories, including anode material (around 110%), Optical Transceiver-SFP (350%) and relays (200%). MeitY Secretary S. Krishnan said the scheme has already exceeded both its investment and production targets. "The investment target was Rs 59,350 crore, while the approved investment has already reached Rs 69,548 crore," he said. Similarly, against the targeted production of Rs 4,56,500 crore, the approved projects are now expected to generate production worth Rs 5,34,101 crore. "We are yet to reach the employment target, but we expect that to increase shortly," Krishnan added. Krishnan said ATL's lithium-ion cell units at Rewari and Sonipat are already operational, while several other major projects are nearing commercial production. Tata Electronics' enclosure plant in Hosur is expected to become operational soon, while Kaynes' PCB plant near Chennai is likely to begin production within the next month. Dixon's display and camera module facility is expected to become operational within four months. Motherson's enclosure plant in Kanchipuram and Wipro's laminate plant are likely to start operations within the next two to three months. Yuran Technologies, part of the Foxconn Group, is developing an enclosure facility in Kanchipuram that is expected to become operational within six months. Secure Circuits' PCB facility is also likely to go live within the same period. Krishnan noted that these include several large-ticket investments, with one project involving an investment of nearly Rs 21,000 crore. "The overall target set by the Hon'ble Prime Minister is to achieve $500 billion in electronics production by 2030. We are confident that we can achieve this target," Krishnan said. articles.title: India's first Vande Bharat sleeper depot takes shape in Jodhpur - The Hans India
articles.content: India’s first Vande Bharat sleeper depot takes shape in Jodhpur Naresh Nandam Update: 2026-08-18 03:35 IST Divisional Railway Manager Anurag Tripathi Jodhpur: The Jodhpur Railway Division of the North Western Railway is setting up India’s first maintenance depot dedicated to Vande Bharat sleeper trains, said Divisional Railway Manager Anurag Tripathi. In an interaction with press representatives from Andhra Pradesh at his office in Jodhpur on Monday, Anurag Tripathi informed that the first phase of the depot is almost complete and it’s operations are expected to start soon. He said that the government plans to build four such depots across the country in the first phase to cover different geographical areas, and the Jodhpur depot is placed at a location that will serve the North-Western region, covering trains that run through Delhi, Jaipur, Ajmer, Barmer, and Ahmedabad. He said that the Vande Bharat sleeper trains maintained at this depot will not be restricted to running only within the Jodhpur division. They may operate across different divisions but will come back to Jodhpur for their regular maintenance. Though two Vande Bharat express trains are connecting Jodhpur to Delhi and Ahmedabad, he said that there are no specific proposals at present to start new Vande Bharat sleeper routes from Jodhpur. On the construction, Tripathi said the depot is being built at in two phases. The first phase is nearly complete and was being built at a cost of around Rs 140 crore. The second phase will require an investment of about Rs 100 crore, and it will take about one to one and a half years to complete after starting of the work. The DRM informed that the depot is being developed through a joint venture with a Russian technology partner. He said the private partner had initially suggested a build and operate model, but Indian Railways decided to keep full ownership of the infrastructure. Indian Railways is providing the entire investment for the basic infrastructure, which includes laying tracks, building the joint sets, and constructing the core facilities. The Russian partner will bring in and operate their advanced technology on site. He further said that the depot will have the Kavach anti-collision system, advanced wheel alignment and setting systems, dedicated wheel lathe lines, pit lines, and sick lines. The sick lines will work like a hospital for trains that need major repairs. Advanced cranes designed to handle the components of Vande Bharat trains will also be installed, he added. On staffing, Tripathi said the depot will be run by a combined team of existing Indian Railways staff and supervisory staff brought in by the private partner. The existing railway staff will move from maintaining standard trains to this new facility. He assured that mandatory training programmes will be organised for all nominated railway staff to make them fully ready to handle and maintain the advanced systems of the Vande Bharat sleeper trains.
